info.description:
## Overview

The Journeys API is the part of the Scope API a sensor, a connector and a console use: the operations tagged `journeys` with every schema they reach, and nothing else. HTTP success records or reads facts; it does not mean the stitcher has run.

## Resources

Installs and their keys, policy and probes (`createInstall`, `readInstall`, `updateInstall`, `createInstallKey`, `readInstallPolicy`, `readInstallProbe`), the policy versions an install pins (`listPolicies`, `createPolicy`, `updatePolicy`), the request records as the sensor ships them (`createRequests`, a batch whose idempotency key is each record's own id) and the debugger's read of them (`listRequests`), what the stitcher derives (`listJourneys`, `readJourney`, `listVisits`, `readVisit`, `listIntents`, each join with its confidence label), the other ways in (`createConnector`, `deliverConnector`, `verifyConnector`, `createAccountEvents`) and the ways out (`createDestination`, `updateDestination`, `createWebhookEndpoint`, `updateWebhookEndpoint` with the events of the `webhooks` section, `createDataExport`, `createTaskProposals`, `decideTaskProposal`, and the console's read-only MCP server, `mcp`).

## Rules

- Every write carries an `Idempotency-Key`; reuse it after an ambiguous response.
- Every error is a typed code in the error envelope; unknown states fail closed.
- The contract version travels in `x-scope-contract-version`; the whole Scope API is `openapi.json`.
info.title: Scope Journeys (the public API's Journeys resources)

### Use when
Register one sensor deployment: from `init` with no account yet (the install waits in the system tenant behind a seven-day claim link) or from the console for a customer.

### Preconditions
- A stable UUIDv4 Idempotency-Key (the CLI mints one per init run)
- Without a session, at most five unclaimed installs per address per hour

### Durable effect
Mints the install, its key (returned once, absent under the OIDC form) and, when unclaimed, the claim link; with a session the install is created claimed to the customer.

### This response does not mean
An unclaimed install records traffic but stitches nothing until it is claimed; the key is never shown again.

### Next endpoint
`readInstallPolicy`

### Common conflicts
- 429 when the address created five installs in the hour

### Example
`POST /v1/installs`

parameters.description: Stable UUIDv4 command identity for idempotent Campaign commands.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

201.description: The install, its key once (absent under OIDC), the claim link while unclaimed, and the files init writes.

409.description: A mismatched x-scope-contract-version is rejected with incompatible_contract.

429.description: Five unclaimed installs were created from this address in the hour.

common_conflicts: 429 when the address created five installs in the hour
x-scope-flow.durable_effect: Mints the install, its key (returned once, absent under the OIDC form) and, when unclaimed, the claim link; with a session the install is created claimed to the customer.
x-scope-flow.not_complete: An unclaimed install records traffic but stitches nothing until it is claimed; the key is never shown again.
preconditions: A stable UUIDv4 Idempotency-Key (the CLI mints one per init run)

post.description:
### Use when
Exactly one of: claim the install with its token, pin or unpin a policy, revoke it, or advance its salt epoch by one.

### Preconditions
- A console session
- A stable UUIDv4 Idempotency-Key

### Durable effect
The claim moves the install and every record it shipped into the customer's tenant and marks the stitch due; a pin changes the policy the sensor fetches within a minute; a revocation stops the key for good; the epoch bump is recorded for the sensor's next policy fetch.

### This response does not mean
The claim answers when the install row moved; a large backlog of records keeps moving in batches behind it. A revocation keeps the records.

### Next endpoint
`readInstall`

### Common conflicts
- 410 claim_expired after seven days
- 403 claim_invalid on a wrong token
- 409 already_claimed
- 422 policy_foreign for another customer's policy
- 422 salt_epoch_sequence when the epoch is not current plus one

### Example
`POST /v1/installs/{install_id}`

parameters.description: Stable UUIDv4 command identity for idempotent Campaign commands.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

403.description: The principal is not authorized, or the claim token is wrong (claim_invalid).

404.description: No install with that id exists for this principal.

409.description: A mismatched x-scope-contract-version is rejected with incompatible_contract.

410.description: The claim link expired (claim_expired): run init again or ask for a new link.

422.description: The policy belongs to another customer (policy_foreign) or the epoch is not current plus one (salt_epoch_sequence).

- A console session

### Use when
Read one policy version with its document; expand[]=counts adds the would-apply counters per rule and install environment inside `since` (seven days by default, 30 at most).

### Preconditions
- A console session

### Durable effect
None, a read.

### This response does not mean
The document is what a sensor fetches; a rule's `mode` says whether it changes anything on the wire. The counters are the decisions stamped on this version's requests: `would_apply` is what a dry-run rule would have done, `skipped` a rule its environments[] excluded.

### Next endpoint
`updatePolicy`

### Common conflicts
- 404 for a version of another customer
- 400 since_out_of_range: since reaches back more than 30 days
- 400 expand_unknown: an expansion other than counts

### Example
`GET /v1/policies/{policy_id}?expand[]=counts&since=2026-10-03T00:00:00Z`

200.description: The version and its document, with the would-apply counters when expand[]=counts was asked for.

post.description:
### Use when
You are a sensor shipping a batch of request records and declarations after the response went out: up to 500 objects, up to 4 MB, gzip accepted.

### Preconditions
- The install's key as the bearer, or the Vercel OIDC token of an install bound at init
- Each record's id is a UUIDv7 the sensor minted

### Durable effect
Writes the batch as received to the journeys-ingest bucket, then the accepted records as rows; a record whose id already exists is accepted and not inserted. Marks the customer's stitch due.

### This response does not mean
202 means the batch is stored, not stitched: journeys and visits follow within a minute. `rejected` names the elements refused by index and reason; `warnings` the duplicates and an outdated observer.

### Next endpoint
`readInstall`

### Common conflicts
- 413 when the body passes 4 MB (16 MB inflated)
- 429 with Retry-After when the tenant's daily quota is spent
- 503 when the raw batch could not be stored: retry once, then drop and count

### Example
`POST /v1/requests`

202.description: The batch is stored: the accepted count, the elements rejected by index and reason, the warnings.

409.description: A mismatched x-scope-contract-version is rejected with incompatible_contract.

413.description: The batch passes 4 MB as received or 16 MB inflated.

429.description: The customer's quota is exhausted (batches per minute, or records per day; an unclaimed install's own, smaller limits); the message names the quota and the limit, Retry-After says when; nothing was stored.

503.description: The raw batch could not be stored; nothing was inserted. Retry once.

post.summary: Ship a batch of request records (the sensor's write)

common_conflicts: 413 when the body passes 4 MB (16 MB inflated)
429 with Retry-After when the tenant's daily quota is spent
503 when the raw batch could not be stored: retry once, then drop and count
x-scope-flow.durable_effect: Writes the batch as received to the journeys-ingest bucket, then the accepted records as rows; a record whose id already exists is accepted and not inserted. Marks the customer's stitch due.
x-scope-flow.not_complete: 202 means the batch is stored, not stitched: journeys and visits follow within a minute. `rejected` names the elements refused by index and reason; `warnings` the duplicates and an outdated observer.
preconditions: The install's key as the bearer, or the Vercel OIDC token of an install bound at init
Each record's id is a UUIDv7 the sensor minted
x-scope-flow.use_when: You are a sensor shipping a batch of request records and declarations after the response went out: up to 500 objects, up to 4 MB, gzip accepted.
